Series::StatAccessor::normc¶

Back to Series::StatAccessor API Reference

Signatures¶

Series Series::StatAccessor::normc() const
Series SeriesStatProxy::normc() const

What It Does¶

normc() scales each column to Euclidean length one. For matrix column c, it computes c / ||c||_2; zero columns stay zero. This is useful when columns are feature vectors whose direction matters but raw magnitude should not.

For a vector, there is only one lane, so normc() and normr() both normalize the whole vector. Their distinction becomes meaningful at rank two and above.

Returns And Call Styles¶

The output is floating-point, out-of-place, and shape-preserving. The direct x.stat.normc() and explicit proxy x.stat().normc() calls select the same operation.

Examples¶

Example 1. Columns are normalized independently.

auto x = pluss::make_series({{3.0, 4.0}, {0.0, 5.0}});
std::cout << x.stat.normc() << "\n";

Output¶

pluss::Series(shape=[2,2], strides=[2,1], dtype=float64, platform=cpu, numel=4, contiguous=true)
data=[[1, 0.62469505],
  [0, 0.78086881]]

Column zero divides by 3, while column one divides by sqrt(41). This is why the same matrix produces different numbers under normr().

Example 2. Summing squared components down dim=0 verifies unit column norms.

std::cout << x.stat.normc().square().sum(0) << "\n";

Output¶

pluss::Series(shape=[2], strides=[1], dtype=float64, platform=cpu, numel=2, contiguous=true)
data=[1, 1]

Column zero has norm 3; column one has norm sqrt(41). Dividing by those separate lengths produces the displayed values.

Choosing Rows Or Columns¶

Use normr() when each row is an observation or embedding to normalize as a unit. Use normc() when each column is the independent vector. The operation is identical mathematically; only lane membership changes.

Gotchas And Failure Modes¶

  • normc() does not remove column means.

  • Zero columns remain zero and cannot become unit vectors.

  • Transposing, applying normr(), and transposing back expresses the same geometry.

See Also¶

  • normr: row-wise Euclidean normalization.

  • center: remove offsets without changing spread.
